counterexample: Let k=1 and work with smooth real-valued functions. Take the two equations Ix=0 and Dx=0, i.e. x=0 and x'=0. Applying the induction hypothesis to the first k=1 equation leaves x=0 (with ψ=true). Combining this new equation with the extra equation x'=0 again produces a system of exactly two equations. Its size is 2, which is not less than k=1; indeed it is the same two-equation problem being proved. Thus the proposed recursive application makes no progress and is circular.
assessment_summary: Steps 0002–0003 follow from the stated induction hypothesis. Step 0004 falsely claims that the resulting two-equation system has size less than k and can therefore be handled inductively. The explicit k=1 case disproves this claim, so the suggested induction does not establish the result.
